thread:
Marta (Marketing): final call — announce for tomorrow 09:00 PT. need: changelog link, docs canonical url, canary timing, and inbound lead routing. low lift items only. who can pick what?
Jin (PMM): I can own the public post and benchmark blurb. will need the benchmark dashboard link and the final top-line stat.
Aaron (Eng PM): I'll drop the release notes link and canary plan. landing page + canary will be deployed with the release.
Priya (Docs): docs live but i need the canonical url (we have both /docs and /guides). prefer /docs/serve/adaptive-batching as canonical. can add anchors for quick links.
Kai (Eng): canary questions — what's the traffic ramp you want? also, any fallback model variant for drop-in degradation?
Marta (Marketing): target: social post at 09:05 PT, blog at 09:10 PT, webinar follow-up email at 09:30 PT. want 5–10% traffic canary for first 15m, rollback if error rate >2% or latency >2x baseline. fallback = small-quant model (v1.2-q4).
Aaron (Eng PM): changelog link: https://redwood.internal/releases/17765 — snippet below (use in marketing post):
```
- Adaptive batching: 20–40% cost reduction for small sync requests
- KV-cache prefix sharing for improved cold-start latency
- New routing policy: region-pref, cost-fallback
```
Jin (PMM): perfect — i'll use the first two bullets in the benchmark narrative. where's the benchmark dashboard?
Kai (Eng): dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/17765 — baseline vs canary graphs. i'll pin the key chart (p99 latency) for you.
Priya (Docs): canonical doc url set: https://docs.redwood.com/docs/serve/adaptive-batching — updated TOC and added anchors: #overview, #benchmark, #rollout, #troubleshooting
Marta (Marketing): inbound leads routing: confirm HubSpot form id and webhook? we want to route enterprise leads to AE queue, trials to onboarding flow.
Aaron (Eng PM): HubSpot form id: 8943. webhook endpoint for immediate routing: https://hooks.redwood.com/leadrouter/v1/ingest — form will POST with tags: {"source":"announce","tier":"trial|enterprise"}. (Ops added CORS + auth token)
Priya (Docs): added a short QA section on the doc about the canary fallback and the rollback steps, with exact commands:
```bash
# rollback to fallback model
retool deploy --model v1.2-q4 --route adaptive-batching
```
Kai (Eng): canary plan: 10% for 15m -> 30% for 45m -> 100% if metrics green. monitoring hooks to PagerDuty at error_rate > 1.5% and latency_p99 > baseline*1.8. I'll attach the runbook to the release notes.
Marta (Marketing): Jin — please finalize benchmark copy and include link to dashboard + a screenshot. Priya — push the canonical doc link into the blog and social assets. Aaron/Kai — confirm the canary windows in the release config.
Jin (PMM): will do. suggested headline: "Adaptive batching cuts per-request costs without trading latency" — i will A/B headline with two variants in draft.
Aaron (Eng PM): release config: canary windows set in CI: `canary: [ {percent:10, duration:15m}, {percent:30, duration:45m} ]`. will push before midnight PT.
DeployBot: deploy scheduled by Aaron at 2026-03-10T16:00:00Z — job id 57721. :rocket:
Marta (Marketing): final checklist before publish: 1) blog + social draft approved ✅ 2) changelog link in post ✅ 3) docs canonical url in all CTAs ✅ 4) canary config confirmed ✅ 5) lead webhook test ✅ 6) benchmark screenshot ready ✅
Priya (Docs): i've added /docs anchor to the blog draft and QA'd the snippets. ready for review.
Kai (Eng): prod test of webhook routing succeeded (test payload ok).
Jin (PMM): i'll post at 09:05 PT and ping this channel when live. please react with :thumbsup: when you see it.
Aaron (Eng PM): triple-checked the rollback commands in the runbook. also added a temporary rate-limit increase for canary to avoid throttling.
Marta (Marketing): thanks team — if anything blocks, call out here. otherwise see you tomorrow for launch. :partyparrot:
